seo.the-eighteen-job-families-of-the: The eighteen job families of the hrmforce Skills Framework, each with a base profile inherited by the jobs in that family.
ui.every-job-in-this-family-inherits: Every job in this family inherits this profile and deviates from it with a limited number of additions, adjustments and removals. The target levels below apply to the medior level.
ui.these-values-are-added-to-every: These values are added to every target level of the family and then clamped to 1 to 5.
ui.every-skill-in-this-profile-sorted: Every skill in this profile, sorted by weight. The behavioural anchor under each skill belongs to the target level.
ui.the-same-profile-with-the-job: The same profile with the job family seniority adjustment applied. Target levels are clamped to 1 to 5.
ui.anchors-sit-at-n1-n3-and: Anchors sit at N1, N3 and N5. N2 and N4 are deliberately not anchored: raters interpolate between them, following the O*NET convention.
ui.the-validities-are-the-corrected-meta: The validities are the corrected meta-analytic estimates from Sackett, Zhang, Berry and Lievens (2022) in the Journal of Applied Psychology, which replace the older Schmidt and Hunter (1998) figures. The spread matters as much as the mean: with a high SD, validity varies strongly by context.
ui.agree-the-profile-with-the-hiring: Agree the profile with the hiring manager before the first candidate is measured. Weights shifted afterwards make the outcome indefensible.
ui.choose-the-assessment-method-per-skil: Choose the assessment method per skill from the Assessment method column. Combine at most three methods per candidate.
ui.calibrate-the-assessors-in-a-two: Calibrate the assessors in a two-hour session using the anchors in chapter 5. Anchors without rater training deliver little.
ui.fill-in-the-match-calculator-and: Fill in the match calculator and discuss the gaps in the development conversation. Type A and type G are selection criteria, not one-quarter development goals.
ui.enter-candidate-levels-and-see-the: Enter candidate levels and see the fit, the gaps and the knockouts.
ui.search-for-a-job-or-a: Search for a job or a skill. You immediately see the profile, the competencies to measure, and which hrmforce questionnaire does that. The fully evidenced profile is available as a download.
seo.pick-a-job-and-calculate-the: Pick a job and calculate the fit of a candidate or employee against the profile online. Weighted fit, gaps per skill and knockouts, with nothing stored.
ui.open-a-job-and-click-calculate: Open a job and click Calculate the match there, or go straight to the calculator for one of these common jobs.
ui.performing-above-the-target-level-doe: Performing above the target level does not count extra, because overqualification is not a better match. The advice bands are a working agreement, not a psychometric constant.
seo.how-the-hrmforce-skills-framework-is: How the hrmforce Skills Framework is built: five layers, five skill types, a proficiency scale with behavioural anchors, and an assessment method with validity evidence per skill.
ui.high-level-reporting-and-the-layout: High-level reporting and the layout of a skill passport.
ui.the-conversation-level-with-the-clien: The conversation level with the client: which clusters matter for this job.
ui.the-unit-of-measurement-assessment-me: The unit of measurement. Assessment method, instrument, weight and behavioural anchor attach here.
ui.the-search-layer-granular-terms-as: The search layer: granular terms as they appear in vacancies and CVs. They inherit the assessment route of their construct.
ui.assessment-and-the-development-conver: Assessment and the development conversation. Anchors at N1, N3 and N5.
ui.why-two-skill-layers-you-cannot: Why two skill layers: you cannot provide behavioural anchors and validity evidence for thousands of terms. The constructs therefore remain the unit of measurement, while the granular layer makes the whole thing searchable and matches vacancy text.
ui.name: Name
ui.five-levels-instead-of-seven-or: Five levels instead of seven or eight, because rater reliability barely improves above that while usability in a conversation declines. The four dimensions come from SFIA 9, and defining levels by cognitive demand, task complexity and autonomy follows DigComp 3.0.
ui.every-skill-has-a-primary-assessment: Every skill has a primary assessment method. The validities are the corrected meta-analytic estimates from Sackett, Zhang, Berry and Lievens (2022) in the Journal of Applied Psychology. They replace the Schmidt and Hunter (1998) figures, which came out systematically too high because of an excessive range restriction correction.
ui.the-spread-matters-as-much-as: The spread matters as much as the mean. Above an SD of .18 validity varies strongly by context and local validation is needed. Think in incremental validity and method combination, not in rankings.
ui.the-mapping-is-conceptual-and-not: The mapping is conceptual and not formally validated. Where a reference could not be justified the field was left empty rather than inventing a plausible code.
ui.not-a-standard-every-profile-is: Not a standard. Every profile is a starting point to be tailored with the organisation before selecting on it.
ui.not-a-decision-rule-a-fit: Not a decision rule. A fit score supports a conversation. Always combine it with a structured interview, the strongest single predictor.
ui.not-a-normed-measurement-there-are: Not a normed measurement. There are no norm groups per skill yet: a level is a definition, not a percentile.
ui.not-a-replacement-for-rater-training: Not a replacement for rater training. Behavioural anchors only work well alongside a calibration session for the assessors.
ui.this-is-a-selection-criterion-not: This is a selection criterion, not a short-term development goal. Do not put a three-month development plan on it.
ui.n2-and-n4-are-deliberately-not: N2 and N4 are deliberately not anchored. Raters place them between the anchors, following the O*NET convention.
ui.source-note: Source: {framework}, version {version}, built {built}. Crosswalks to ESCO v1.2.1, O*NET 31.0, Lightcast Open Skills, SFIA 9, DigComp 3.0, EntreComp, LifeComp, GreenComp, AILit, WEF Future of Jobs 2025, ISCO-08 and the Dutch CBS occupational classification BRC 2014 edition 2025. This profile is a starting point, not a standard: align it with your own organisation before selecting on it.
